_note: Clearance register. verdict must be CLEAR before any pipeline stage may use a source. Verified 2026-08-17 against primary licence text. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-anatomy-atlas-spec.md section 9.
_tier: B+ : nothing named in the slice viewer or catalog; one credit line on the RadioAnatome info screen; third-party notices in Settings > Legal.

visible-human.licence: US Government work, no copyright; NLM download Terms and Conditions apply
visible-human.credit: Courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine
visible-human.note: Licence agreement requirement was dropped in 2019. The credit obligation is contractual (from the download T&C), not copyright.

wikimedia-cc0.note: Only files whose extmetadata License is pd or cc0. Keep the extmetadata blob per file as an audit record; Commons tags are user-asserted and sometimes wrong.

totalsegmentator-total.licence: Apache-2.0 (code and the total / total_mr weights)
totalsegmentator-total.note: Run on our own PD images ONLY. Never run on the CC BY 4.0 training dataset, so nothing shipped is an adaptation of it.

totalsegmentator-open-subtasks.licence: Apache-2.0 (the subtask weights NOT marked with an asterisk in the upstream subtask list)
totalsegmentator-open-subtasks.note: Only the 18 tasks in the package's own `commercial_models` register need a licence; everything else carries the same Apache-2.0 grant as `total`. Verified in code, not inferred: totalsegmentator.registry.requires_license(task) is literally `task in commercial_models`, and it returns False for headneck_bones_vessels / head_muscles / teeth / abdominal_muscles / craniofacial_structures / vertebrae_body / trunk_cavities, True for appendicular_bones / brain_structures / tissue_types / thigh_shoulder_muscles. An earlier note in this project wrongly treated ALL subtasks as gated. Upstream also warns these are trained on smaller datasets than `total`, so expect them to be less robust — which is what the HU verification step is for. Run on our own PD images ONLY.

fastsurfer-segonly.note: --seg_only (asegdkt, cereb) needs NO FreeSurfer licence. The SURFACE pipeline does; never invoke it. Weights licence as distinct from code is UNVERIFIED, and its training labels are FreeSurfer-derived.

synthseg-v1.note: v1.0 ONLY. The 2.0 / robust / parc weights come from a separate link with no licence statement: UNVERIFIED, do not use. Take from GitHub, never from a FreeSurfer bundle.

grays-1918.licence: Public domain in the US (published before 1931)
grays-1918.note: Source from an ORIGINAL 1918 scan. NOT Project Gutenberg (trademark notice + 20% commercial royalty clause). NOT Wikisource wikitext (editor annotations are BY-SA). EU/UK status unclear until 2035 if W. H. Lewis is editor of record.

terminologia-anatomica-terms.licence: Individual terms are explicitly public domain
terminologia-anatomica-terms.note: TERMS ONLY. The TA2 document is CC BY-ND: never redistribute the PDF or a wholesale copy of its hierarchy.

spl-nac-brain-atlas.note: 300+ hand-labelled structures; highest-quality single source. Part B 1(b) notice goes in Settings > Legal.

fsl.blocking_clause: Non-commercial. Clauses (2)/(3) reach the DEVELOPMENT PROCESS: using FSL to generate coordinates for a commercial product is caught even if no FSL code ships.

jhu-icbm-dti-81.blocking_clause: Distributed under the FSL licence; independent non-FSL terms UNVERIFIED. This is why named white matter is hand-authored.

freesurfer.blocking_clause: Part B 1(b) forces MGH-prefaced licence text into user documentation. Also states clinical applications are neither recommended nor advised. Use fastsurfer-segonly instead.

tcia.blocking_clause: No CC0 collection found. CC BY 4.0 s3(a) attribution plus a mandatory DOI citation.

fma.blocking_clause: CC BY attribution. Licensor's own page is offline; version taken from OBO Foundry, so PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED.

uberon.blocking_clause: CC BY attribution. The LICENSE file is unambiguous even though GitHub's detector reports NOASSERTION.

wikipedia.blocking_clause: Attribution plus share-alike, which would force our derived text under BY-SA.

mindboggle-101.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (paper) vs CC BY 4.0 (site) - conflicting
mindboggle-101.blocking_clause: Unresolved conflicting licence claims; under the paper's version it is non-commercial AND share-alike. Encumbers the DKT40 classifier.

totalsegmentator-brain-structures.licence: Proprietary; free for non-commercial, paid commercial licence required
totalsegmentator-brain-structures.blocking_clause: Paid commercial licence required (free academic key is not usable under the commercial goal set 2026-08-19). 16 brain substructures. BUT buying it probably does NOT solve the brain: the blocker measured on our data is the SOURCE, not the model — a 33-slice 4 mm cadaver T1 defeated SynthSeg, which ran clean and still returned ~2x L/R asymmetry with most of the brain unlabelled. Fix the data first (see openneuro-cc0), then FastSurfer --seg_only, already CLEAR, is expected to suffice without any purchase.

totalsegmentator-appendicular-bones.licence: Proprietary subtask weights; free licence for non-commercial use, commercial requires contacting the author
totalsegmentator-appendicular-bones.blocking_clause: COMMERCIAL LICENCE REQUIRED, and the FREE ACADEMIC KEY IS NO LONGER SUFFICIENT: the owner reversed to a commercial goal on 2026-08-19, so the academic/non-commercial key cannot be used. A paid commercial licence must be bought from jakob.wasserthal@usb.ch. This is the ONLY route to tibia, fibula and patella (the knee): the free `total` task has femur only, and VISTA3D/NV-Segment-CT was checked against its own label_dict.json and has NO tibia, fibula or patella either. Alternative needing no licence at all: a classical threshold-plus-position segmenter, which is what already ships for the thorax.
totalsegmentator-appendicular-bones.note: Owner asserts StewardMD is non-commercial and accepts that determination. Recorded here because the register is the audit trail, not the conversation.

autopet-fdg-petct.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (NIfTI via FDAT) or TCIA Restricted (DICOM via TCIA)
autopet-fdg-petct.attribution: required: Gatidis S, Kuestner T, University Hospital Tuebingen, plus DOI citation
autopet-fdg-petct.blocking_clause: BANNED BY OWNER 2026-08-19: RadioAnatome is to be COMMERCIALLY deployable, and CC BY-NC 4.0 forbids that for as long as the data ships. Owner instruction: no CC BY-NC, research-only or restricted datasets, and PET/CT is to be kept architecturally separate for a later, separately licensed phase. Supersedes the earlier non-commercial position recorded on the same day.
autopet-fdg-petct.note: Only whole-body PET/CT found that is redistributable at all. HEALTHY-TOTAL-BODY-CTS was checked and rejected: its segmentations are CC BY 4.0 but the CT IMAGES sit under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy (facial-reconstruction risk), so they cannot ship. No PD or CC0 whole-body PET/CT exists as of 2026-08-19.

radiopaedia.blocking_clause: Non-commercial only. Free-to-students distribution inside a commercial app does not qualify.

totalsegmentator-dataset.attribution: required: one credit line plus the Zenodo DOI
totalsegmentator-dataset.note: THE SINGLE BIGGEST UNLOCK FOUND. 1228 CT volumes of real LIVING clinical patients across many scanners, institutions and pathologies, WITH 117 anatomical structures already expertly labelled. CC BY 4.0 permits commercial use AND redistribution of the images and of derivatives, with attribution. This needs NO segmentation model and NO model licence: the masks are supplied, so liver, spleen, kidney, lung, muscle, vessels and cardiac structures become available WITHOUT buying anything. It also fixes the real problem, which is that Visible Human is a frozen cadaver: living tissue has normal HU, so lung reads -700 to -850 instead of -540, organs separate on contrast, and muscle reads +20 to +70 instead of the -13 to -21 measured in our pelvis. CAVEAT: these are clinical studies chosen for pathological variety, so near-normal volumes must be CURATED by a clinician before use as an anatomy reference. Distinct from the existing rule against RUNNING the model on this dataset: shipping the CC BY 4.0 images and labels directly is a different and legitimate route that costs only an attribution line.

openneuro-cc0.licence: CC0 1.0 Public Domain Dedication (OpenNeuro default for uploaded datasets)
openneuro-cc0.note: THE BRAIN ANSWER, and it costs nothing. OpenNeuro releases data under CC0 by default, which places no restrictions on who may use it or for what, commercial included. ds003563 is a whole-brain in-vivo T1 at 250 um isotropic from a LIVING subject - far better than the 1 mm the brain pipeline needs, and the exact opposite of the 33-slice 4 mm cadaver T1 that defeated SynthSeg. Paired with fastsurfer-segonly (already CLEAR) this is expected to yield real brain labels with NO purchase. Verify the specific dataset's own licence field before ingesting: CC0 is the default, not a guarantee, and a few datasets opt out.

nv-segment-ct.licence: Code Apache-2.0; weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial-friendly)
nv-segment-ct.note: VISTA3D. Investigated on request. Licence is fine and it is commercially usable, but it adds NOTHING we lack: checked against its own vista3d/data/jsons/label_dict.json, its skeleton is humerus 87/88, scapula 89/90, clavicula 91/92, femur 93/94, hip 95/96, sacrum 97, skull 120, sternum 122, vertebrae 33-56 - i.e. the same set as the free `total` task - with NO tibia, fibula or patella, and 'brain' as a single undifferentiated class (22). Its weights are also trained on 11454 living, often contrast-enhanced volumes, so on a frozen cadaver its priors are WRONG in the same way TotalSegmentator's were when it put muscle labels on fat. No reason to switch. Marked CLEAR so it may be used, not because it should be.

nv-segment-ctmr.blocking_clause: Non-commercial weights, so barred by the commercial goal set 2026-08-19. Would otherwise have been the most tempting option on the table: 345+ classes including 50 MRI body classes and 133 brain substructures. Not usable.
